findings.title: Java MessageFormat syntax breaks i18next interpolation in the account console
findings.body: The account console (keycloak.v3, React) translates messages with i18next. Every other key in this file uses `{{0}}`, `{{1}}` placeholders. The user-profile error handler passes server params as `{0: ..., 1: ..., 2: ...}` and calls `t(key, params)`. This change switches `error-invalid-multivalued-size` to Java MessageFormat (`{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}`) and adds a ChoiceFormat sub-pattern, which i18next supports in neither case. Users who violate a multivalued attribute's size constraint will see the raw string `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` instead of a formatted message. Keep `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}` here, or use i18next pluralization.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat/ChoiceFormat syntax breaks i18next interpolation in the admin console
findings.body: The admin console (keycloak.v2) renders server-side user-profile validation errors client-side via i18next (`setUserProfileServerError` → `t(errorMessage, {0:..,1:..,2:..})`), which expects `{{n}}` placeholders. The previous value used `{{0}}`/`{{1}}`/`{{2}}`. The new value uses `{0}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`, so i18next leaves them unreplaced. Admins will see the literal pattern text when a multivalued attribute size validation fails.

findings.title: Lithuanian file now contains an Italian sentence
findings.body: `totpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is the Italian translation (apparently copied from messages_it). Lithuanian users will see Italian text in the OTP setup step. It should be a Lithuanian sentence such as `Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:`.

findings.title: Lithuanian login file now contains an Italian sentence
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with the Italian text `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`. Lithuanian users configuring OTP on the login page will see an Italian instruction. The original Lithuanian content should have been rewritten in Lithuanian rather than replaced by another locale's string.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text placed in the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
findings.body: The new `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式) and was likely copied from zh_TW. The rest of this zh_CN file uses Simplified Chinese, e.g. `mobile=手机` on the line above. It should be the Simplified form, e.g. `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`.

findings.title: Common prefix/suffix computation can overlap and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body:
The suffix loop only bounds `end` by the string lengths, not by `length - start`. So the common prefix and suffix can overlap in the shorter string. Example: value `

a

`, sanitizer output `

a

`. Here `start` = 8 and `end` = 4, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` becomes `substring(8, 4)` and throws. Duplicated closing tags are exactly the kind of malformed input this verifier should report. Instead the plugin crashes with an unhandled runtime exception and no useful message. Bound the suffix loop with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

findings.title: ChoiceFormat contents are removed before sanitizing, so HTML inside them is never checked
findings.body: For `linkExpirationFormatter.timePeriodUnit*` and `error-invalid-multivalued-size`, every `{n,choice,...}` block is replaced with `...` before the sanitizer runs, for both the translation and the English value. A translation such as `{0,choice,0#|1#x}` would pass verification untouched. These are server-rendered messages in email and login themes, so this defeats the purpose of the check for those keys. Split each choice alternative and sanitize it individually, or only strip the `n<`/`n#` selector syntax, instead of discarding the whole block.

findings.title: Anchor-mismatch message omits file and key
findings.body: `Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string` contains neither the key nor the file path, unlike the duplicate-key and illegal-HTML messages. When the plugin runs over hundreds of property files in the build, a maintainer cannot tell which file or key to fix. Include `key` and `file` in the message; `key` is already passed into `santizeAnchors` but unused.

findings.title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a raw RuntimeException
findings.body: The English file path is derived by string replacement on the absolute path. If that file does not exist (a new theme/locale layout, a path whose naming doesn't match the regex, or a file outside the expected directories), `verifySafeHtml` throws an unchecked `RuntimeException`. `verify()` only catches `IOException`, so the exception is not converted to a `MojoExecutionException`. The Maven build fails with a stack trace instead of a reported verification problem.

findings.title: No test that a valid translation produces no findings
findings.body:
All new tests only assert that some error message is present (`hasItem(...)`). Nothing verifies that a legitimate translation passes cleanly: identical anchors, allowed `/

/
` tags when the English source has HTML, `{{0}}` placeholders, choice formats, or `<0>` numeric tags. A verifier that flags everything would pass this suite, and false positives that break the build on valid translations would go unnoticed.
